
# Module 9: Performance & Memory {#mod-perf}

---

### Measure Before You Optimize

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```python
import timeit
import cProfile
import pstats
import tracemalloc

# 1. Micro-benchmarking syntax
timeit.timeit("sum(range(1000))", number=10_000)

# 2. Memory leak detection
tracemalloc.start()
run_agent_pipeline()
current, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
print(f"RAM Peak: {peak / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB")
tracemalloc.stop()

# 3. CPU profiling
cProfile.run("main()", "agent.prof")
stats = pstats.Stats("agent.prof")
stats.sort_stats("cumtime").print_stats(10)
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Profiling Strategy
- **Wall Time vs CPU Time:** In agent runtimes, 95% of wall-clock time is spent waiting on external model sockets. Standard CPU profilers can be misleading.
- **Distributed Traces First:** Inspect request traces and network spans before refactoring Python loops.
- **Golden Rule:** Measure, identify the bottleneck, optimize that specific hotspot, and benchmark again to verify.
:::
:::

### Caching and Memory Optimization

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```python
from functools import cache, lru_cache
from dataclasses import dataclass

# Unbounded memoization for immutable static schemas
@cache
def load_tool_json_schema(tool_name: str) -> dict:
    ...

# Bounded LRU cache for document embeddings
@lru_cache(maxsize=1024)
def compute_text_hash(text: str) -> str:
    ...

# Memory-efficient dataclasses with __slots__
@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)
class StreamMessage:
    role: str
    content: str
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Memory Best Practices
- **Bounded Caches:** Unbounded caches (`@cache`) on unbounded user inputs cause catastrophic memory leaks in 24/7 agent servers. Always bound with `@lru_cache(maxsize=N)`.
- **Hashable Arguments:** Functions memoized by `@cache` require all arguments to be hashable (strings, tuples, frozen dataclasses).
- **Never Cache Side Effects:** Never memoize functions that write to databases, trigger emails, or alter agent state.
:::
:::

---

### Choosing a Concurrency Model

| Workload Type | Recommended Architecture | Engineering Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Many network I/O calls** | **`asyncio`** | Low-overhead tasks waiting on remote sockets |
| **Blocking legacy libraries** | **`threads` / `to_thread`** | Keeps main asyncio loop responsive |
| **CPU-heavy parsing / vector math** | **`multiprocessing`** | Bypasses GIL; distributes compute over CPU cores |
| **Isolated parallel Python** | **`subinterpreters` (3.14)** | Isolated memory and interpreter states in one process |
| **Threaded parallel compute** | **Free-threaded (3.14)** | True multi-core execution on modern hardware |

> **Default Stance:** Always start with **`asyncio`** for agent systems. Reach for processes or threads only after measuring a clear CPU bottleneck.

---

### Performance in Agent Applications

::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Parallel Tool Calls
Run independent model tool calls concurrently using `asyncio.TaskGroup` instead of sequentially.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Stream Everything
Stream tokens immediately to reduce user-perceived latency (TTFT) from seconds to milliseconds.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-important}
### Reuse Connections
Maintain a shared `httpx.AsyncClient` connection pool to eliminate repeat TLS handshakes.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
### Budget Tokens
Prune conversational history, truncate repetitive tool outputs, and enforce strict token ceilings.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="34%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Cache Pure Lookups
Memoize unchanging prompt templates, tool schemas, and document embeddings.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Monitor Tail Latency
Track **p95 and p99 latency** metrics; average latency hides stalling agent tasks.
:::
:::
:::
